title: Telnet service exposed on local and upstream interfaces
evidence: Nmap showed 23/tcp open on management interface. The service returned Login as:.
impact: A local network attacker may reach the Telnet-like login service. If weak or hardcoded credentials exist, this may allow remote administrative or shell access.
recommendation: Disable Telnet by default and replace it with SSH only if remote administration is required.
cwe: CWE-319 (Cleartext Transmission) / CWE-259 (Hardcoded Password)
threat_scenario: In a threat environment, an attacker connected to the Wi-Fi or upstream network can perform automated dictionary attacks (such as Mirai-style brute force) or sniff cleartext administrative commands.
hardening_coverage:
1. Remove the telnetd daemon from startup scripts.
2. Block inbound TCP port 23 across all network interfaces.
3. Enforce cryptographic SSH authentication.

title: Web interface allows login without user-supplied credentials
evidence: HTTP GET request to status.html directly returns administrative dashboard without requiring authentication.
impact: The login page does not require the user to input credentials, allowing anyone on the network to click LOGIN and access the admin dashboard.
recommendation: Require users to configure and enter a unique administrator password during initial setup.
cwe: CWE-306 (Missing Authentication for Critical Function) / CWE-287 (Improper Authentication)
threat_scenario: Any unauthenticated attacker on the local Wi-Fi network can bypass authentication and access router management.
hardening_coverage:
1. Require mandatory user-defined password on initial onboarding.
2. Reject empty password authentication.
3. Disable bypass routes.

title: Default admin credentials exposed in login page HTML
evidence: index.html contains hidden username value admin and hidden password value admin.
impact: The login page reveals hidden username and default password values to anyone inspecting the client source.
recommendation: Remove hardcoded credentials from client-side HTML.
cwe: CWE-798 (Use of Hardcoded Credentials) / CWE-200 (Exposure of Sensitive Information)
threat_scenario: An attacker inspecting client-side HTML or automated crawlers can immediately harvest default credentials.
hardening_coverage:
1. Remove all hardcoded default credentials from client-side HTML.
2. Authenticate credentials strictly server-side.

title: Admin credentials stored in Base64 Authorization cookie
evidence: Browser storage shows a cookie named Authorization starting with Basic. HttpOnly and Secure are false.
impact: The cookie can expose admin credentials because Base64 is not encryption and the cookie lacks HttpOnly and Secure flags.
recommendation: Use secure server-side session tokens with HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite attributes.
cwe: CWE-312 (Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information) / CWE-1004 (Sensitive Cookie Without 'HttpOnly' Flag)
threat_scenario: Any client-side script (XSS) or network eavesdropper can decode plaintext admin credentials directly from the cookie header.
hardening_coverage:
1. Implement cryptographically random session tokens.
2. Set HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite=Strict flags.

title: DNS resolver exposed on management interface
evidence: Port 53 UDP/TCP responds to DNS queries on management interface and intercepts setup domain lookups.
impact: The device runs an active DNS resolver which may redirect setup queries or expose internal DNS resolution.
recommendation: Restrict DNS exposure to required client interfaces only and validate redirect behavior.
cwe: CWE-345 (Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity) / CWE-400 (Resource Amplification)
threat_scenario: Outdated DNS daemon can be targeted for DNS Cache Poisoning (DNSpooq) to redirect connected users to phishing servers.
hardening_coverage:
1. Upgrade dnsmasq to version 2.83+.
2. Bind DNS listener exclusively to internal LAN.

title: No logout option to terminate admin session
evidence: status.html shows management options but lacks an explicit logout button or session invalidation endpoint.
impact: Users cannot explicitly terminate the admin session from the interface, leaving administrative access open indefinitely.
recommendation: Add a logout function that clears and invalidates the session token on the server.
cwe: CWE-613 (Insufficient Session Expiration)
threat_scenario: Administrative sessions persist indefinitely on shared browser sessions.
hardening_coverage:
1. Add a dedicated logout button invalidating session tokens.
2. Enforce 10-minute idle session timeouts.

title: Admin credentials exposed in URL query parameters during login
evidence: Login submission triggers HTTP GET with CMD=USERLOGIN&username=admin&pcPassword=admin.
impact: Credentials may be stored in browser history, proxy server logs, screenshots and network packet captures.
recommendation: Use HTTP POST method over TLS encryption for all authentication requests.
cwe: CWE-598 (Use of GET Request Method with Sensitive Query Strings) / CWE-319 (Cleartext Transmission)
threat_scenario: Administrative passwords are permanently logged in intermediate HTTP proxy logs, router gateway histories and packet sniffers.
hardening_coverage:
1. Transition form action method to HTTP POST.
2. Transmit credentials within an encrypted payload body.

title: Public firmware updates and vendor support unavailable
evidence: Online firmware discovery across official vendor portals, support archives and device mirrors returned zero valid updates.
impact: The device manufacturer does not provide an official firmware update repository or public security patches, leaving known vulnerabilities unpatchable.
recommendation: Select hardware from established manufacturers that provide regular, digitally signed firmware security updates.
cwe: CWE-1277 (Firmware Not Updateable) / CWE-1059 (Incomplete Documentation and Support)
threat_scenario: Newly disclosed kernel or service vulnerabilities cannot be patched, leaving the hardware permanently exposed.
hardening_coverage:
1. Establish automated over-the-air (OTA) update infrastructure.
2. Enforce cryptographic signature verification on all firmware images.

title: Web management interface served over unencrypted HTTP
evidence: Management portal is reachable on TCP port 80 without automatic HTTPS redirection or TLS encryption support.
impact: All web interactions, login attempts and configurations are sent in plaintext and vulnerable to local eavesdropping.
recommendation: Enable HTTPS management interface with modern TLS (1.2/1.3) encryption.
cwe: CWE-319 (Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information) / CWE-352 (Cross-Site Request Forgery)
threat_scenario: An attacker on the same local wireless channel can sniff credentials, cookies and session tokens.
hardening_coverage:
1. Deploy embedded TLS web server (such as uHTTPd with wolfSSL/mbedTLS).
2. Redirect HTTP port 80 to HTTPS port 443 automatically.
